Released on 2026-07-23.

Breaking changes

  • Ruff now enables a much larger set of rules by default (413, up from 59). See the blog post for more details and the new Default Rules page for a full listing of the enabled rules. Sourced from prek's releases.

0.4.11

Release Notes

Released on 2026-07-25.

Highlights

  • This release adds two new builtin hooks, deny-pattern and require-pattern, as native alternatives for pygrep use cases. deny-pattern fails when a configured pattern is found, while require-pattern ensures every selected file contains a match. By matching natively without spawning a Python subprocess, they run over 4x faster than pygrep in benchmarks. Note that they use Rust regex syntax, which does not support look-around features such as negative lookbehind.

  • prek run now supports --glob <PATTERN> to run hooks on tracked files matching a glob. It can be repeated or combined with --files and --directory.

  • Hook priorities now support reusable aliases:

    [priorities]
checks = 10

    [[repos]]
repo = "builtin"
hooks = [
{ id = "check-json", priority = "checks" },
{ id = "check-yaml", priority = "checks" },
]

    This makes parallel scheduling easier to read and maintain.

Sourced from pytest's releases.

9.1.1

pytest 9.1.1 (2026-06-19)

Bug fixes

  • #14220: Fixed a logic bug in pytest.RaisesGroup which would might cause it to display incorrect "It matches FooError() which was paired with BarError" messages.
  • #14591: Fixed a regression in pytest 9.1.0 which caused overriding a parametrized fixture with an indirect @​pytest.mark.parametrize to fail with "duplicate parametrization of '<fixture name>'".
  • #14606: Fixed list-item typing errors from mypy in @pytest.mark.parametrize <pytest.mark.parametrize ref> argvalues parameter.
  • #14608: Fixed a regression in pytest 9.1.0 where conftest.py files located in <invocation dir>/test* were no longer loaded as initial conftests when invoked without arguments. This could cause certain hooks (like pytest_addoption) in these files to not fire.

9.1.0

pytest 9.1.0 (2026-06-13)

Removals and backward incompatible breaking changes

  • #14533: When using --doctest-modules, autouse fixtures with module, package or session scope that are defined inline in Python test modules (not plugins or conftests) will now possibly execute twice.

    If this is undesirable, move the fixture definition to a conftest.py file if possible.

    Technical explanation for those interested: When using --doctest-modules, pytest possibly collects Python modules twice, once as pytest.Module and once as a DoctestModule (depending on the configuration). Due to improvements in pytest's fixture implementation, if e.g. the DoctestModule collects a fixture, it is now visible to it only, and not to the Module. This means that both need to register the fixtures independently.

Deprecations (removal in next major release)

  • #10819: Added a deprecation warning for class-scoped fixtures defined as instance methods (without @classmethod). Such fixtures set attributes on a different instance than the test methods use, leading to unexpected behavior. Use @classmethod decorator instead -- by yastcher.

    See 10819 and 14011.

  • #12882: Calling request.getfixturevalue() <pytest.FixtureRequest.getfixturevalue> during teardown to request a fixture that was not already requested is now deprecated and will become an error in pytest 10.

    See dynamic-fixture-request-during-teardown for details.

  • #13409: Using non-~collections.abc.Collection iterables (such as generators, iterators, or custom iterable objects) for the argvalues parameter in @pytest.mark.parametrize <pytest.mark.parametrize ref> and metafunc.parametrize <pytest.Metafunc.parametrize> is now deprecated.

    These iterables get exhausted after the first iteration, leading to tests getting unexpectedly skipped in cases such as running pytest.main() multiple times, using class-level parametrize decorators, or collecting tests multiple times.

    See parametrize-iterators for details and suggestions.

  • #13946: The private config.inicfg attribute is now deprecated. Use config.getini() <pytest.Config.getini> to access configuration values instead.

    See config-inicfg for more details.

  • #14004: Passing baseid to ~pytest.FixtureDef or nodeid strings to fixture registration APIs is now deprecated. These are internal pytest APIs that are used by some plugins.

v8.2.0 🌈 New inputs quiet and download-from-astral-mirror

Changes

This release brings two new inputs and a few bug fixes.

New inputs

Lets talk about the new inputs first.

quiet

Pretty simple. It turns of all info loggings. Useful if you use this in a composite action and are not interested in all the details. In the upcoming releases we will add log groups to fully implement support for "less noise"

[!NOTE]
Warnings and errors are always logged.

download-from-astral-mirror

In some cases you may want to directly use the fallback of checking for available versions and downloading releases from GitHub instead of using the astral.sh mirror. Setting download-from-astral-mirror: false allows you to do that.

Bugfixes

When using the astral.sh mirror to query available versions and download releases (done by default) we now stop sending the GitHub token in the header. The mirror never looked at it but we shouldn't be handing out that data even if it is just a short lived token. title: Refactor: v2.0.0 - Full Project Restructure

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

body:
## Summary

This PR represents a complete ground-up refactor of `HEACalculator`, bumping the version to 2.0.0. The old monolithic architecture has been replaced with a modular src/ layout, modern Python tooling, and comprehensive test coverage. Recent commits have added enhanced thermodynamic calculations (Miedema parameters), improved GUI components, and refined documentation.

### What Changed

#### Project structure
  - Migrated from a flat `HEACalculator/` layout to a `src/HEACalculator/` src-layout with proper package separation
  - Replaced `setup.py` / `setup.cfg` / `requirements.txt` with `pyproject.toml` + `uv` for dependency and build management
  - Added `pre-commit` configuration with `ruff` for linting and formatting

#### Core rewrite
  - Split the original monolithic `HEA.py` (~675 lines) into focused modules: `composition.py`, `thermodynamics.py`, `models.py`, `hea.py`, `helpers.py`, `converter.py`, and `exceptions.py`
  - All thermodynamic properties on `HEAThermodynamics` are now cached_property for lazy, single-computation access
  - Data layer migrated from inline Python dicts to JSON-backed modules (`elements.json`, `mixing_enthalpy.json`, `formation_enthalpy.json`)
  - Added Allen electronegativity (CE scale) to element data and thermodynamic calculations
  - Added Miedema mixing enthalpy and structural enthalpy calculations with dedicated `MissingMiedemaDataError` exception
  - Added Goldschmidt CN12 corrected atomic radius to atomic properties database
  - Custom exceptions introduced: `ElementNotFoundError`, `MissingMixingEnthalpyError`, `MissingFormationEnthalpyError`, `MissingMiedemaDataError` (base: `MissingPairDataError`)

#### CLI
  - Replaced the old CLI with a Typer-based interface supporting `single`, `range`, and `csv` subcommands under a search group
  - GUI is now launched via a dedicated `gui` subcommand

#### Shared utilities (`utils.py`)
  - Introduced `utils.py` as a shared layer consumed by both the CLI and the GUI, replacing the previous arrangement where the GUI imported a helper directly from `cli.py`
  - `find_all_comps()` moved from `cli.py` to `utils.py` and rewritten: the old two-step approach (combinations_with_replacement + permutations with set deduplication) is replaced by a direct recursive generator (`_gen_compositions`) that yields each valid ordered composition exactly once with no duplicate work
  - Pure single-element compositions (one element at 100 at%, the rest at 0 at%) are now included in range search results when both 0 and 100 fall naturally within the specified range — previously these were unconditionally excluded

#### Solid Solution Prediction
  - **Refined solid solution prediction models** with updated criteria and improved accuracy
  - Enhanced test coverage for prediction logic

#### Thermodynamic Enhancements
  - **Miedema parameters and structural enthalpy calculations** integrated into thermodynamic computations
  - Improved atomic properties database with additional radius corrections and electronegativity measures
  - Better handling of missing data scenarios with dedicated exceptions

#### Testing
  - Replaced the two original test files with a full pytest suite across `tests/core/`, `tests/data/`, `tests/test_cli.py`, `tests/test_app.py`, `tests/test_main.py`, and `tests/test_utils.py`
  - `find_all_comps` tests moved from `test_cli.py` to `test_utils.py` and extended with behavioral coverage for pure single-element inclusion and exclusion
  - Comprehensive tests for custom exception classes
  - Tests for Miedema enthalpy calculations and GUI result-table configurations
  - Reference alloy for tests is FeCoCrNi

#### CI/CD
  - Added GitHub Actions workflows for linting, testing, documentation deployment (GitHub Pages), release to PyPI, and Dependabot dependency updates

#### Documentation
  - Migrated from Sphinx to MkDocs Material
  - New pages: installation guide, usage guide, API reference, FAQ, and troubleshooting
  - API reference updated to document `utils.find_all_comps`
  - Usage guide notes that pure single-element compositions are included in range searches spanning 0-100 at%

#### Breaking Changes

  - Package is now installed from `src/` layout; import paths are unchanged but the internal module structure is entirely new
  - All data access now goes through `Element("Fe")`, `MixingEnthalpy(("Fe", "Co"))`, and `FormationEnthalpy(("Fe", "Co"))` factory calls backed by JSON files
  - `find_all_comps` is now importable from `HEACalculator.utils`, not `HEACalculator.cli`
  - Range searches now include pure single-element endpoints; results sets may be larger than with v1 for searches spanning the full 0-100 at% range
